div.b: The order the pieces have to arrive in
div.span:
1 Deployment profile and license
2 IAM: superuser, or a custom role
3 Network Channel, if the target is private
4 Target, validated end to end
5 Scan

A private target cannot validate until the channel
is ONLINE, and a scan cannot start until the target
is VALIDATED.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 789px; margin-left: 957px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Worth saying out loud to the customer
div.span:
Nothing is installed in front of the application and
nothing changes about how its real users reach it.
The platform behaves like any other API client
holding a credential.
What does change: attack prompts arrive at a
production-shaped endpoint for hours at a stretch.
Agree the window, the rate limit, and who is
watching the alerts.
